steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Given circumstances: the facts of the play — time, place, situation, relationships. An actor must know these before they can act truthfully. | Key Fact: Magic if: 'What would I do if I were in this situation?' — helps the actor find truthful reactions, not fake 'acting'. | Key Fact: Emotion memory: recalling a personal emotional experience to fuel a scene's emotional truth — not reliving, but using the memory. | Key Fact: Units and objectives: breaking a scene into beats (units), each with a specific objective — gives structure and purpose to every moment.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how an actor would use Stanislavski's 'magic if' and 'given circumstances' to prepare for a role. | What is subtext and why is it important in naturalistic performance? Give an example. | Compare Stanislavski's approach to Brecht's — how do they differ in their relationship with the audience?
